proposals.title: Closing-Line Calibrated Probability as a Single High-Signal Feature
proposals.source: MDPI Information 17(1):56 — Uncertainty-Aware ML for NBA Forecasting (Jan 2026)
proposals.rationale: Isotonic-regression-calibrated closing moneyline implied probabilities form a near-optimal probabilistic baseline. This single feature often outweighs hundreds of box-score features in Brier score contribution. Post-hoc isotonic regression on XGBoost outputs against holdout set directly optimizes Brier. Estimated gain: -0.008 to -0.015 Brier.
implementation: Add closing_ml_implied_prob column to game rows (from data/full-odds-2025-26.json ml_home odds)
Apply isotonic regression: from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression, fit on 70% train holdout
Use calibrated_prob as Cat 55 feature in engine.py
Also post-process island outputs via calibration wrapper

proposals.title: Rest/Travel/Back-to-Back Feature Audit and Completion
proposals.source: Scientific Reports 2025, doi:10.1038/s41598-025-13657-1 — stacked ensemble NBA
proposals.rationale: The Sci Reports 2025 stacked ensemble paper (L1: XGB+LGB+RF → L2: LR, 77.5% accuracy) found that top-3 SHAP features across all model types were: home_next (next game home indicator), team_elo_5y (5-year Elo decay), and team_elo. Models without explicit rest-days and back-to-back travel distance features underperformed by ~0.008 Brier. CNN Brier=0.221 closed the gap to <0.21 by adding these 3 families. Our S15 at 0.22034 has a CNN gap of only 0.00034 — rest/travel features are likely the marginal improvement path.
implementation: Audit feature_names in S15 gen=1521 population for: rest_days_diff, b2b_flag_home, b2b_flag_away, travel_miles_7d
If missing, add to engine.py Cat 2 (game context) or Cat 5 (schedule features)
travel_miles: use team arena lat/lon + haversine for last away game

proposals.title: TabPFN-2.5 as Meta-Feature Stacking Layer
proposals.rationale: TabPFN-2.5 (Nov 2025) handles ~100K rows and ~2000 features, beating tuned XGBoost on TabArena. The winning technique from DrivenData PREPARE challenge 2025: use TabPFN-2.5 to generate soft probability outputs ('meta-features') as input columns for XGBoost. In-context learning acts as a strong stacking layer without retraining. Typical stacking gain on sports datasets: -0.005 to -0.015 Brier.
implementation: Colab T4 experiment: train TabPFN-2.5 on 80% of 9551 games
Extract 2-class probability vector [P(home_wins), P(away_wins)] for all games
Add tabpfn_prob_home as new feature in Kaggle karpathy loop
Benchmark: TabPFN-standalone vs XGBoost+TabPFN_meta vs XGBoost_baseline
